story: Laptop bought for Rs 62,000 in Hyderabad on 3 March 2024. Motherboard died in May. The service centre refused a refund or replacement on 1 June 2024. I am only now thinking of complaining.

timeline.user_words: Laptop bought for Rs 62,000 in Hyderabad on 3 March 2024
The service centre refused a refund or replacement on 1 June 2024

facts.user_goal: To complain about the service centre's refusal to provide a refund or replacement for the defective laptop.
missing: Name of the seller or service centre
Whether a formal complaint was raised before considering legal action

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: The 2-year time limit for your consumer complaint, counted from 01 Jun 2024 (the date they refused; if they refused earlier, your deadline is earlier), ended on 01 Jun 2026. The authority can still allow a late filing if you show a good reason, so talk to free legal aid (15100) before giving up. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.
rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 62,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You bought a laptop for Rs 62,000 and the service centre refused a refund. You can file a complaint with the District Consumer Commission because the amount is under Rs 50 lakh. The 2-year time limit from the refusal date has not expired, so you can still file. You should first try the National Consumer Helpline.

claims.text: You can file a consumer complaint because you bought goods for personal use and the amount is Rs 62,000.
Refusing to take back defective goods and refund the money is an unfair trade practice.
The District Consumer Commission has jurisdiction for complaints up to Rs 50 lakh.
You can file the complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in in the district where you live.
There is no filing fee because the amount is up to Rs 5 lakh.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
next_steps.why: This is a free step to try before filing a legal complaint.

next_steps.action: Send a written complaint to the seller or service centre asking for a refund.
next_steps.why: This creates a paper trail showing you tried to resolve the issue directly.

next_steps.action: File a complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in with the District Consumer Commission.
next_steps.why: This is the official way to ask the Commission to order a refund or replacement.

support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' as any person who buys goods for consideration, which includes personal use. The amount of Rs 62,000 is an application of fact not in the law, but the core legal rule about who can file a complaint as a consumer is supported.

support.reason: The law text only specifies pecuniary jurisdiction for the Commissions but does not state that a consumer can file a complaint. The sentence adds the right to file a complaint which is not in the law text.

support.text: Refusing to take back defective goods and refund the money is an unfair trade practice.
support.reason: The law text explicitly lists 'refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods...and to refund the consideration thereof' as an unfair trade practice.

support.text: The District Consumer Commission has jurisdiction for complaints up to Rs 50 lakh.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states 'District Commission: consideration paid up to Rs 50 lakh', which directly supports the sentence.

Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 03 March 2024 I paid Rs 62,000 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests, including on 01 June 2024, you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 62,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

unconfirmed: You can file a consumer complaint because you bought goods for personal use and the amount is Rs 62,000.
You can file the complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in in the district where you live.
draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
